content: Individuals who are candidates for metabolic surgery are at an increased risk of developing substance abuse, depression, anxiety, and suicidal ideation. This risk is particularly significant if these mental health issues worsen following the surgical procedure. It is essential that all candidates undergo a comprehensive mental health evaluation conducted by a professional with expertise in obesity management prior to surgery. If unresolved substance abuse problems or severe mental health conditions are identified, the surgery should be postponed until these issues are adequately addressed. Both preoperative and postoperative psychological assessments are crucial to ensure the safety and overall well-being of the patient throughout the surgical process.
